description: B1 · 60 min. Small talk before a meeting: openings, follow-ups, and how to leave politely.

exercises.name: Today's goal
exercises.html: By the end of this lesson you can start, keep and end a short conversation with a colleague — without awkward silence.

exercises.instruction: Match the phrase with its meaning

exercises.text: Watch: small talk before a meeting

exercises.instruction: Watch again and decide: true or false
statements: The speaker starts with a question about the weekend.
She says the office is quiet in December.
She ends the conversation with “have to run”.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the words from the box
sentences: — Busy, but good. We [moved] to a new flat.
— Oh, nice! How [come] you chose that area?
— Sorry, I [have] to run — meeting in two minutes.

lines: — [By the way*/In the way/On the way], did you get my email?
— I [have to run*/have run/have running] now, talk later!

exercises.instruction: Sort into two groups: opens a chat / ends a chat

words: a work discussion with a time

questions.q: A colleague says “How's it going?”. Best reply?
You want to leave. What do you say?
options: Sorry, have to run — talk later!

exercises.html: Tell your teacher about the last small talk you had at work: who, about what, how it ended.

exercises.instruction: Write 5 sentences: how you would start and end a chat with a new colleague
Record 90 seconds: small talk with a colleague before a meeting
